newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Metrobank slips 1.8 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Metrobank slips 1.8 pct in late trade.

text.p: Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co (Metrobank) dipped 10 pesos, or 1.8 percent, to 545 pesos in late Thursday trade despite a denial that one of its debtors, San Carlos Milling Co, was in financial troubles, traders said.
"People are probably not convinced by their explanation. And they may be thinking that if there is smoke, there is fire," said Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president at Philippine Asia Equity.
Both Metrobank and San Carlos have denied the rumours saying that the 1.1 billion pesos in loans of the sugar miller are active and well-covered by its 1.85 billion pesos worth of collateral.

"Our market is driven by sentiment and despite the denials, there is still the fear. I think investors will soon lighten up and the issue will hold above the 535 pesos level," said Lawrence de Leon, analyst at Dharmala Securities.
Metrobank, an index heavyweight, was the second most actively traded issue with turnover of 172.95 million pesos late in the session.
